Lauren / Marissa / Samir —

Draft sizing notes based on the sample:

1) Baseline assumptions we used:
- Peak RPS: 420
- Average tokens/request: 450 (prompt+response)
- Low-latency portion: 35% (p99 target < 200ms)
- Concurrent KV-backed workers: 560

2) Recommended footprint (initial reserved commitment):
- Hybrid mix: 6 x H100-equivalent nodes (preferred for latency) + 4 x A100-equivalent nodes for background and batchable workload. This maps to ~10 reserved GPUs with a 30% headroom for unexpected bursts.
- Warm pool: maintain 2 H100-equivalent prewarmed instances per low-latency shard (~4 prewarmed GPU instances total) to keep cold-starts < 50ms for pinned model traffic.

3) Latency and batching tradeoffs:
- For the 35% SLA traffic we route to pinned, non-quantized model on H100s with continuous batching window of 5–10ms and KV affinity; expected p99 ~160–190ms (depends on sequence length).
- For the 65% bulk traffic we recommend batch windows up to 120ms on A100 nodes; this yields large token-efficiency gains and keeps cost down.

4) Model-fallback policy (suggested):
- Tag traffic at the API layer: customer-facing = "pin", background = "flex".
- Under sustained oversubscription (>80% reserved usage for 5m) automatically route "flex" to 8-bit quantized variant on A100 nodes. Notify via webhook and enable auto-rollback when usage drops.
- Documented expected quality delta: empirically ~2–4% BLEU/ROUGE drop on our internal evals for their prompt class; recommend a 2-week canary run before full switch.

5) KV cache and session affinity:
- KV cache sizing: assume average KV per session = 120KB; for 3,800 sessions plan ~450MB warm KV footprint per shard; recommend dedicated Redis cluster with 3 shards for failover and hot cache locality.
- Session affinity: consistent hashing per user id preferred to maintain cache hits and avoid cross-host fetches. Expect ~12–18% improvement in p50 token compute due to cache hits.

6) Next steps & artifacts for procurement:
- Proposed commitment: 10 reserved GPUs, 12-month term with quarterly usage flex buffer.
- Deliverables: cost estimate, SLA draft, fallback playbook, and an action item list for on-call runbook.

I'll assemble a one-pager and a spreadsheet mapping GPU SKUs to expected cost and SLOs and share by Monday AM. If procurement needs accelerated pricing for Oct 7 we can produce the initial estimate today — LMK.
